items.title: Woman arrested after baby’s body found in Kuala Berang drain missing head, hand; gender unknown
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Oct 18 — Police have arrested a local woman to assist in investigations into the discovery of a baby’s body in a drain at the Padang Setengge residential area near here on Friday afternoon. Hulu Terengganu police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the 23-year-old suspect was arrested at her residence at 3.30pm for investigation under Section 318 of the Penal Code. Bernama reported yesterday that a woman discovered the body of a baby with several missing limbs in a drain while washing clothes behind her house in the Padang Setengge residential area.

items.title: 'Football will never be the same without my brother,' says teen after fatal lorry accident
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 14-year-old boy was left traumatised after witnessing his 8-year-old brother being struck and killed by a lorry while retrieving a football in Kampung Surau Haji Daud yesterday. Muhammad Idham Najmi Mohd Asizol said he could only cry when he saw his younger brother, Muhammad Atihff Zriqqiz, lying on the road. The Form Two student of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Tengku Ismail said he had been playing football with Atihff and their 12-year-old brother, Muhammad Ammar Najwan, inside their fenced compound at about 3pm.

items.title: Three-year-old boy dies after fall from 11th floor in Sepang
items.summary: Sepang district police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said his team received a report regarding the incident at 5.54am today. “The victim, a Malay boy, was confirmed dead at the scene,” he said in a statement yesterday. Norhizam said the investigation paper was opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001.

items.title: Five held after luxury home in Iskandar Puteri allegedly used to scam Singaporeans
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 18 — A luxury house in Iskandar Puteri allegedly used as a call centre to lure Singaporeans into fake investments has been raided, with five suspects arrested. Police seized electronic devices worth more than RM100,000, while investigations continue. Johor recorded 9,897 scam investigation papers involving RM212.6 million in losses between January and September this year, with an average of 37 scam reports filed daily, state police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said.

items.title: #NSTviral: Boy wins hearts for guiding blind elderly man at LRT station
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A young boy has won hearts online after he was seen guiding a blind elderly man at Maluri LRT station, helping him navigate the station safely. Threads user @syifanadine92 shared the moment, praising the boy's kindness. One user, @careyryan_, recounted helping a blind man exit an MRT station despite being late for a train.

items.title: Pasir Gudang records country's highest API reading at 190, 25 areas unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in the country at 190, as 25 areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality as of 8am today. In the Klang Valley, Johan Setia recorded 163, followed by Shah Alam (161), Klang (159), Petaling Jaya (157), and Banting (156). In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded 156, and Batu Muda registered 155, while Putrajaya logged 159.

items.title: 'My sister's face looked peaceful,' says brother of murdered Customs officer
items.summary: TUMPAT: "Although there were slight wounds on the side of her face, she looked peaceful," said the brother of Norhazwani Ibrahim, who was believed to have been killed by her husband in Nilai, Negri Sembilan, last Thursday. Mohd Hazwan Ibrahim, 38, said he was overcome with emotion when he saw his sister's face for the final time after her shroud was opened. "Her face looked calm.

items.title: Man, 52, found dead in drain near Taman Ciku in Bukit Mertajam
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 18 — The body of a 52-year-old man was found in a drain near Taman Ciku here yesterday. The discovery was reported to the authorities at about 4.30pm, prompting firefighters to head to the scene to recover the body, The New Straits Times reported. His body was taken to Bukit Mertajam Hospital for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.

items.title: Haze: Schools, educational institutions in Johor to close for another five days from tomorrow
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 18 — The Johor government has extended the closure of schools and educational institutions across the state for another five days from tomorrow (October 19) due to the haze. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following a meeting of the Johor Haze Management Coordination Committee at noon yesterday. He said the extension would remain subject to developments in air quality, weather forecasts and ongoing health assessments.

items.title: Trump paused Russia sanctions to 'analyse' impact on global economy: Rubio
items.summary: JOINT BASE ANDREWS: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump's waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to "analyse" their impact on the global economy. "The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis.

items.title: Zelenskyy says Trump could lift more Russia sanctions
items.summary: KYIV: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday that he feared the United States would lift more sanctions on Russia and that President Donald Trump's action only "rewards" Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin. Trump heightened a battle with Zelenskyy on Friday when he signed an executive order that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia's energy revenues. Ukraine said at least two people were killed in Russian air strikes on Saturday.

items.title: 19 killed, 25 injured in stampede at India's Durga Puja festival
items.summary: KOLKATA: At least 19 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that occurred during sudden rainfall at a Hindu religious gathering, officials and Indian media said. West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 other people were injured outside a pavilion "in a stampede" at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata. Afterwards medics were seen moving injured people on stretchers, including a police officer, into a local hospital.

items.title: Protecting kids from AI menace
items.summary: Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) chief executive officer Mediha Mahmood said AI tools could be used to turn images of people into sexually explicit materials or deepfake videos in inappropriate situations. It is a manipulated image or deepfake video altered by AI to depict the victim in a sexual or inappropriate manner," she said recently. Mediha said the growing use of AI tools by children is another concern, as unrestricted applications and websites may make it easier to create illicit content.

items.title: Underwater mountains, canyons hold secrets of Malaysia's seas
items.summary: National Hydrographic Centre (NHC) director-general Rear Admiral Dr Najhan Md Said said understanding this hidden terrain was vital to safe navigation, maritime security and sovereignty. Najhan also serves as the vice-chair of the International Hydrographic Organisation — Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans Sub-Committee on Undersea Feature Names, comprising 12 international experts. He said high-resolution bathymetric surveys had mapped extreme depths across Malaysia's maritime domain.

items.title: National Hydrographic Centre seeks legal status to safeguard Malaysia's maritime interests
items.summary: PORT KLANG: Malaysia needs a dedicated national hydrography act to give its hydrographic authority statutory backing and replace a 54-year-old administrative memorandum that can be amended or rescinded by the cabinet. National Hydrographic Centre (NHC) director-general Rear Admiral Dr Najhan Md Said said despite operating for more than half a century and representing Malaysia in the International Hydrographic Organisation (IHO) since 1975, the centre is still relying on a cabinet memorandum produced in 1972. He said an act of Parliament was needed to establish the NHC as the sole national authority responsible for official nautical charting, bathymetric data governance and maritime safety declarations.

items.title: Smoke trail, flames offer clues to Long Lellang helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Examination of the Flying Doctor Service's Bo-105 helicopter engines, and a video of flames and smoke near the rear of its main gearbox captured during the helicopter's final moments near Long Lellang, Sarawak, could help investigators establish what happened, an aviation expert said. This follows the release of the Air Accidents Investigation Bureau's (AAIB) preliminary report yesterday, which found no fault with the crashed helicopter's airframe, maintenance or pilot. Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School Associate Professor Major Dr Mohd Harridon Mohamed Suffian said a thorough examination of the engines was standard procedure to help investigators determine the likely cause of the incident.

items.title: One survey ship falls short of mapping Malaysia's vast maritime domain [WATCH]
items.summary: PORT KLANG: Only 63 per cent of Malaysia's vast maritime domain has been surveyed to modern high-density hydrographic standards, leaving 37 per cent yet to meet the benchmark. National Hydrographic Centre (NHC) director-general Rear Admiral Dr Najhan Md Said said surveying Malaysia's maritime domain was a major undertaking requiring extensive work to build a comprehensive picture of the seabed. He said Malaysia's breakthrough came in 1998, when KD Perantau, a hydrographic survey vessel, began its service.

items.title: Israeli settlers beat French mayor with iron bars, attack European diplomats in West Bank
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy of European diplomats in the West Bank and beat up a visiting French mayor, witnesses said, a day after an American photographer was similarly set upon as violence escalates ahead of bitterly fought elections. The 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France, kicked him and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank alongside the top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats. "I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government," Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, told AFP after he was attacked.

items.title: US demands jail for attackers of American journalist in West Bank
items.summary: JERUSALEM: US Ambassador Mike Huckabee on Saturday demanded that Israel prosecute and jail the assailants in a West Bank settler attack against a Washington Post journalist. "Attacking a female photographer is a despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards," Huckabee wrote on X, taking a far stronger tone than an earlier statement from Washington. Huckabee, a staunch ally of Israel who has nonetheless sharply criticised settler attacks against Americans, did not identify the culprits as settlers, after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu tried to sow doubt as to their identity.

items.title: France protests erupt into looting and fires as 1,200 arrested, 150 police hurt
items.summary: PARIS: Clashes between police and protesters, massive looting and multiple blazes gripped France on Saturday, as nationwide marches against soaring inflation degenerated into street violence of "extreme intensity." Whole streets in Paris "have been devastated", the city's mayor, Emmanuel Gregoire, said as groups of masked young men torched parked cars and ransacked many shops. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who earlier slammed the "violence of extreme intensity", said late Saturday that 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers hurt.

items.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts four drones as Egypt weighs defensive support
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia said on Saturday that it had intercepted a fresh wave of incoming drones, as its ally Egypt weighed sending the kingdom help in defending against repeated attacks from Yemen's Houthis. Riyadh leads a military coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government in its war with the Houthis, and a military spokesman for the Iran-backed group said Saturday that dozens of Saudi strikes over the past day had killed and wounded "numerous" people. Since Yemen's conflict flared back to life in July after a years-long hiatus, Saudi Arabia has faced sustained Houthi missile and drone attacks targeting its oil installations, tankers and transit hubs, including one on Riyadh's airport last week that killed 13 people.

items.title: Indonesian fisherman found off Tioman repatriated
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: An Indonesian fisherman who went missing after becoming separated from the boat carrying his two children has been repatriated after being found adrift in waters off Pulau Tioman, Pahang. The Indonesian Consulate General in Johor Bahru worked with the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Pahang on the search and rescue operation following a missing-person report received by Indonesian authorities. Bachtiar was reported missing on Oct 10 after becoming separated from the boat carrying his two children while they were fishing.

items.title: No explosives found at Klang supermarket after bomb threat
items.summary: KLANG: Police found no explosives or suspicious devices at a supermarket along Jalan Kapar here following an email claiming that such materials had been planted on the premises. North Klang police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received a report at 4.04pm today from a male store manager who had received the email. He said police inspected the premises with assistance from the K9 sniffer dog unit, the Selangor police contingent headquarters' bomb disposal unit, the fire and rescue department and the Klang civil defence department.

items.title: 24 evacuated after floods hit eight Penang houses
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Twenty-four residents were evacuated to a temporary relief centre after heavy rain flooded eight houses in Kubang Semang. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said firefighters assessed the situation near Masjid Kubang Semang after receiving a call at 9pm. The residents were evacuated by police to the temporary relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Seri Penanti, which opened at 8.30pm.

items.title: Clashes erupt in France as protesters vow to make government 'tremble'
items.summary: PARIS: Police and protesters clashed in Paris and other French cities on Saturday, with smoke from fires and tear gas billowing over demonstrations nationwide against high prices ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. In Marseille, France's second-largest city, protesters broke into the town hall, overturning a bust and smashing furniture before being forced out by police, AFP journalists saw. The mayor called for police reinforcements.

items.title: Man found dead in drain in Penang
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police recovered the body of a 52-year-old man from a drain near Taman Ciku here. The body was sent to Bukit Mertajam Hospital for a post-mortem. Police investigations are ongoing.

items.title: Hanoi's famous flowers are driving residents mad with their smell
items.summary: THE star-shaped white blossoms of Hanoi's milkwood trees have inspired songwriters and lovers, but city authorities began cutting them back on Friday after an outcry from residents over their "overpowering" fragrance. The trees are common across much of Asia. "Hoa sua is the signature for Hanoi.

items.title: Six women honoured at YTF Women in Technology Awards 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail, and the Raja Perempuan of Perlis, Tuanku Tengku Fauziah Tengku Abdul Rashid, graced the Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah (YTF) Women in Technology Awards 2026 here today. Also present were the Raja Muda of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail, and the Raja Puan Muda of Perlis, Tuanku Dr Lailatul Shahreen Akashah Khalil, who is also YTF Royal Patron. Aini, a former Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) vice-chancellor, won the grand prize in the Senior Women in Technology category, receiving RM30,000.

items.title: Road to an all-electric car fleet will be bumpier than it looks
items.summary: The fuel outlook is clouded by the fact that some countries are moving faster than others to replace ICE cars with EVs, while others are expanding EV fleets alongside sales of conventional cars. By 2035, DNV projects that over 165 million EVs will be on China's roads, before the total tops 360 million by 2050. North America's fleet of ICE cars is around 290 million, and conventional engines account for around 86 per cent of the total car fleet.

items.title: Kelantan policeman injured in parang attack during anti-drug raid
items.summary: TANAH MERAH: A police corporal was seriously injured after being slashed with a parang by a suspected drug pusher during an anti-drug operation in Kampung Lalang Pepuyu. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the 37-year-old officer suffered a fractured left hand in the 1.35pm incident and was admitted to Hospital Tanah Merah. He said a team from the Kelantan police contingent headquarters' Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID), assisted by personnel from Bukit Bunga and Lalang Pepuyu police stations, raided a house in the village.

items.title: NST Leader: Malaysia cannot arrest its way out of the drug menace
items.summary: Efforts to combat drug abuse must be intensified. To be sure, police must continue to target drug syndicates, traffickers and suppliers. Prevention must begin early.

items.title: Hamzah: Wawasan wants to defend seats won under PN in Melaka
items.summary: JASIN: Perikatan Nasional (PN) wants to defend the seats it won in the previous Melaka election, said Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin. He said if Umno wanted to defend the seats it had won, the same principle should apply to Wawasan. he said.

items.title: Sisi says Egypt ready to defend Saudi Arabia 'if requested'
items.summary: CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that Egypt was ready to defend Saudi Arabia "if requested", as fighting flares between the kingdom and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. Since Yemen's war reignited in July, the Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week. "I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," Sisi said.

items.title: Police debunk claims of Bangladeshis gathering in Bukit Bintang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities have dismissed claims that Bangladeshis recently gathered in Bukit Bintang. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks found that the original video showed New Year celebrations in Bukit Bintang in 2022 and had been edited using artificial intelligence (AI). "The video is old footage showing the Selangor Foundation Building, which is old and worn.

items.title: Woman arrested over baby's body found in Terengganu drain
items.summary: KUALA BERANG: Police have arrested a 23-year-old woman to assist in investigations into the discovery of a baby's body in a drain at the Padang Setengge residential area here yesterday. Hulu Terengganu police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the woman was arrested at her residence at 3.30pm for investigation under Section 318 of the Penal Code. He said the arrest enabled police to establish the circumstances surrounding the birth and the woman's involvement in the incident.

items.title: Boy dies after running onto road to retrieve ball in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 17 — An eight-year-old boy was killed after being struck by a lorry while retrieving a ball that had rolled onto the road in Kampung Surau Haji Daud here this afternoon. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said police received a report from a member of the public at 4.10pm about an accident involving a lorry and a pedestrian. “Preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at about 3.40pm when the lorry driver, travelling from Kampung Surau Haji Daud, struck the victim, who had suddenly run onto the road to retrieve a ball that had rolled onto it.

items.title: Civil Defence Force to run emergency control centres round the clock for monsoon season
items.summary: KLUANG, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) is strengthening its preparedness for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL) by operating its operations control centres around the clock to coordinate emergency responses and disaster relief. APM Deputy Chief Commissioner (Operations) Ghazali Abd Rahman said the move was backed by improved communication systems and closer coordination with agencies on disaster management committees at various levels to address the risks of floods, water surges and landslides. He said communication between the southern, eastern and central zones would be improved to ensure effective coordination and allow personnel from other zones to be deployed to disaster-hit areas.

items.title: Missing father and son found weak after three days in Terengganu forest without food
items.summary: JERTIH, Oct 17 — A father and son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today. Besut police chief Supt Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said the two were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area. Bernama reported earlier today that the father and son had gone missing after entering the forest to search for medicinal roots.

items.title: After another downpour, Lembah Subang resident asks minister to step in over recurring floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Flash floods hit several parts of the Klang Valley after heavy rain this afternoon, as a Lembah Subang resident raised concerns over recurring floods in the neighbourhood, alleging that an unfinished pedestrian walkway project may be obstructing nearby drains. Threads user _anuarlatif said in a post today. Another Threads user, amm.yusopp, also reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.

items.title: Budget 2027: Islamic affairs gets RM3.1b, as minister outlines support for ‘pondok’ schools, imams and halal SMEs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The Madani Government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under Budget 2027 to strengthen Islamic development, including support for religious education institutions and the welfare of religious personnel nationwide. “The Madani Government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for sekolah agama rakyat (community religious schools), tahfiz institutions and sekolah pondok (traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim). Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain (Kafa) teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks , nojas and marbuts , in recognition of their contributions to the community.

items.title: Stop dumping pet fish in lakes, govt warns as alien species wiping out natives in Ampang lake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Alien fish account for 95 per cent of fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir, posing a serious threat to the balance of Malaysia’s freshwater ecosystem. He warned that releasing pet fish into lakes, dams and public waterways when they grow too large or become difficult to care for could harm aquatic biodiversity and threaten the survival of local species. Isham said measures included increasing efforts to catch alien fish, releasing local fish fry to help restore the balance of fish populations and expanding public education to discourage people from releasing pet fish into public waters.

items.title: Penang’s RM420m link road to Silicon Island targets first bridge opening by 2028
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — A total of 202.3 hectares of land have been reclaimed at Silicon Island since reclamation works began in September 2023, marking progress in the development of Penang’s next economic growth hub as of October 2026. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the development was envisioned to complement the state’s semiconductor industry while attracting investments in advanced technology, research and development, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven innovation. In a separate statement, Silicon Island Development Sdn Bhd said the Silicon Island Experience Centre was now open to government agencies, investors, local communities and strategic partners to help them better understand the 931-hectare development.

items.title: Selangor Islamic council denies Jais ‘frame-up’ claims in Nik Nazmi’s khalwat detention, says no one is above the law
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) has denied allegations that the detention of former Setiawangsa MP Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) last Thursday over a khalwat case was an act of persecution or a “frame-up”. Mais chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said Jais had acted on an official complaint and followed established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual. Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department.

items.title: From USJ to Shah Alam, flash floods disrupt Klang Valley roads after afternoon downpour
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Afternoon thunderstorms brought flash floods to several parts of the Klang Valley today, inundating roads and disrupting traffic in Selangor as authorities urged motorists to avoid affected areas. Social media posts reported flooding in USJ 1, USJ 7, Sunway, Ara Damansara, Kota Damansara, Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Baru Hicom and Shah Alam, with motorists warned to plan their journeys carefully. In Shah Alam, the city council warned of rising water levels near the traffic lights at i-City in Section 7 and Padang Jawa in Section 16, advising the public to drive cautiously and avoid affected roads if water levels continued to rise.

items.title: GRS takes its election pitch to Kudat, with Hajiji eyeing 16 parliamentary seats
items.summary: “Cooperation and unity among GRS components as well as our partners in the State Unity Government is vital to ensure a decisive victory for GRS in the coming general election,” said Hajiji, who is GRS Chairman and PGRS President. Besides Hajiji’s keynote address, the six GRS Deputy Chairmen will deliver speeches. Both Members of Parliament lost in the State election in November last year to GRS candidates.­ — Daily Express * Editor’s note: GRS stands for Gabungan Rakyat Sabah; PGRS stands for Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah; PBS stands for Parti Bersatu Sabah; PCS stands for Parti Cinta Sabah; LDP stands for Liberal Democratic Party; PHRS stands for Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah; Upko stands for United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation; and SMJ stands for Sabah Maju Jaya.

items.title: Sarawak polls could be as early as November, says state minister Abdul Karim
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — Sarawak could hold its 13th state election as early as November, with the polling window extending to mid-December, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. Abdul Karim, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief, said the timing would depend on when Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg dissolves the Sarawak Legislative Assembly. The Election Commission (EC) would then determine the polling date in accordance with the law, he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: PKR to field experienced, young and women candidates, says Amirudin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to firm up its direction for the Melaka state election within a week, with candidate selection now in its final stages, coalition election strategy director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today. Amirudin said allowing candidates to gain experience in less favourable constituencies could help build a longer-term plan for PKR and the wider coalition. Party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said Pakatan Harapan would contest more seats overall if PKR’s allocation remained at nine.

items.title: Home minister: 24-hour border watch, jetty demolitions to curb cross-border crime in Kelantan
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — Police are maintaining round-the-clock surveillance along all border routes in Kelantan to curb cross-border crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the directive had been issued to Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat to ensure continuous physical surveillance along the border. He said the investigation papers included witness statements and information gathered throughout the investigation.

items.title: Health Ministry: Over 6,700 officers approved for promotions and acting appointments, including four chopper crash victims
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — A total of 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the Ministry of Health (MOH) have been approved for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15. The move reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to recognise officers’ commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery. In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under MOH’s teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.

items.title: ‘That is not our job’: Amirudin rejects claims PKR plotted khalwat trap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari today denied allegations that the party orchestrated a khalwat case involving former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad to undermine a political rival. Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PKR had never discussed or arranged any plan, privately or publicly, to entrap political opponents, news outlet Harian Metro reported. The allegations surfaced after the Selangor Islamic Religious Department detained two people in Petaling Jaya last Thursday to assist investigations into a suspected khalwat offence.

items.title: KL Immigration to probe alleged irregularities in special pass issuance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department will investigate allegations of irregularities in the issuance of special passes at the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office. Its director, Datuk Hamsha Injau, said the department’s Integrity Division would conduct an investigation to determine the validity of the allegations and that no misconduct would be tolerated. He also advised the public to deal with the Immigration Department through official channels and avoid using unauthorised intermediaries.

items.title: N. Sembilan police: Post-mortem finds border agency officer died from pressure on neck, stab wounds
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 17 — Police said preliminary post-mortem findings showed that pressure applied to the neck caused the death of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer found at a government staff quarters in Nilai. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the finding followed a nearly five-hour post-mortem examination that began at 9.40 am today at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here. “The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two on the abdomen and one on the right cheek,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Malaysian Army to review SOP after serviceman arrested with pistol, ammunition and ketum, says chief
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur. Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army’s continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified. The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.

items.title: MAF reviewing allowances to boost reserve force participation, says Chief of Defence Force
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force. Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces. “Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel,” he said.

items.title: Home minister: Immigration depots facing capacity pressure amid daily enforcement operations
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — Immigration depots nationwide are facing capacity pressures due to daily enforcement operations against undocumented migrants, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said the depots had a combined capacity of about 20,000 people, but the continuous arrival of individuals detained during enforcement operations had led to overcrowding. The increase in detainees is also result of the Immigration Department’s mapping of areas with high concentrations of foreign nationals based on data collected and analysed from enforcement operations nationwide.

items.title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi from party activities for three months from Oct 20 after Jais incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Parti Bersama Malaysia has suspended Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months, effective October 20. “Bersama views this development seriously and takes the position that every issue involving the party’s leadership and members must be addressed appropriately to preserve the party’s integrity, credibility and public confidence,” Syukri Razab said in a statement on behalf of the party. The party stated that the decision was necessary and reasonable, without denying Nik Nazmi’s contributions and commitment to Bersama since the party was relaunched in May 2026.

items.title: Drug abuse among Malaysian under-15s a growing concern, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group. Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.

items.title: Lawyer: Zara Qairina’s mother yet to decide on civil action as inquest nears conclusion
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest. Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action. “For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions.

items.title: Man loses RM363,887 in alleged fake bank auction property scam in Miri
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 17 — A man who intended to buy a property for his family has allegedly been cheated out of RM363,887.49 in a non-existent bank auction property deal. Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement shared on Miri police’s official social media page that the 56-year-old victim lodged a police report at Miri Central Police Station on October 15. “The suspect also offered to manage the purchase process, including the preparation of the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and property title transfer,” said the statement.

items.title: Transport minister: RM1,000 aid for remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers to be paid via EFT
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide will receive the RM1,000 Special Financial Aid directly into their respective bank accounts through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the disbursement through this method would be carried out in the next phase, following the first phase of direct handovers to eligible drivers in several zones. “All the aid will be handed over to those who have been verified as eligible before Deepavali,” he told reporters after the special financial aid presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Sri Pinang here today.
